turns.text: I've got several big fluid-filled blisters on my hand from a burn two days ago and they're in the way of everything. How do I look after them properly?
Why are blisters left intact? What's the fluid and the skin over it doing?
How should I dress them so I can use my hand, and how often should I change the dressing?
If I saw a nurse, what would she do with blisters this size?
What do burns specialists say about draining a large blister — when is it done and by whom?
A friend in a kitchen says non-stick pads and a cotton glove under a nitrile glove got him through. Does that sound right?
Someone else told me to keep the hand raised at night. Does that help with the swelling?
I'm a cook, I can't miss more shifts, and there's no walk-in clinic near me. How do I protect them at work?
What do I do if one bursts on its own, and what signs mean infection?
Can you give me a plan — dressing, protection at work, what to do if one bursts, and when to get seen?
